q.intro.text: The left pan holds half a bag and two thirds of a marble. The right pan holds a third of a bag and one marble. They balance: one half x, plus two thirds, equals one third x, plus one.

q.ask.text: Fractions are fiddly. Multiply every term by six. Which equation do you get? Pick one, and say how sure you are.

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the balance moves first, then the notation.

e.step0.text: The pieces are halves and thirds. Six is the least number that both two and three go into, so times six clears every fraction.

e.step1.text: Six copies of each pan: still level, because both pans grew six times. The pieces make whole things: three bags and four marbles balance two bags and six marbles. Three x plus four equals two x plus six.

e.step2.text: Take two bags and four marbles off both pans. One bag balances two marbles. x equals two.

e.step3.text: Put two into the original equation. Both sides are five thirds. So x equals two is right.

e.why.text: Quick check: why may we multiply every term by six?

e.why.ok.text: Yes. Multiplying every term on both sides by the same number, not zero, keeps the balance, and the solution.

e.why.only.text: Twelve or eighteen would clear them too. Six is just the least, so the numbers stay small.

e.why.some.text: Then the right pan would get only its pieces copied, and the balance tips. The one is a term too: it becomes six.

t.intro.text: Now three fourths x, plus one half, equals one fourth x, plus three. The multiplier is found for you: the pieces are quarters and halves, so times four.

t.line.text: Multiply every term by four. Which line do you get?

t.line.ok.text: Yes: times four on every term, both pans. Watch the four copies gather into whole things.

t.line.some.text: Watch: the three marbles were not copied, so the balance tips. The three is a term too: four times three is twelve.

t.line.left.text: Only the left pan was copied, so the balance tips. Both sides get times four.

t.x.text: One bag balances how many marbles? What is x?

t.x.all.text: Ten balances both bags. One bag balances one share: split ten into two.

t.x.no.text: Count one share: ten marbles split into two equal rows.

t.x.ok.text: Yes: ten divided by two is five. x equals five.

t.check.text: Check in the original: what is the left side, three fourths times five, plus one half?

t.check.derived.text: Seventeen is the left side of the line after times four. Check in the original: three fourths times five, plus one half.

t.check.no.text: Three fourths times five is fifteen fourths. Add two fourths. What do you get?

t.check.ok.text: Seventeen fourths, and the right side is seventeen fourths too. x equals five is right.

q.cb.right.text: At the start you picked three x plus four equals two x plus six, and you were right: every term, both sides, the whole number too.

q.cb.one.text: At the start you picked three x plus four equals two x plus one. The one was left out. A whole number is a term too: it gets times six as well.

q.cb.xonly.text: At the start you picked three x plus two thirds equals two x plus one. Only the x terms were multiplied. Every term gets times six.

q.cb.none.text: Multiply every term on both sides by the same number. Then the balance, and the solution, stay the same.

p.intro.text: Maya clears the fraction in two thirds x, plus four, equals six, by multiplying by three. She writes two x plus four equals eighteen, so x equals seven. Is Maya right?

p.test.text: Let's test it. Build the argument, and see where it leads.

p.build.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.no.whole.text: That is exactly Maya's slip. Clearing multiplies every term, so the four must become twelve.

p.no.derived.text: It solves her line, but her line is not equivalent to the original. Check in the original: two thirds of seven, plus four, is not six.

p.no.other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line. Which reason makes this line true?

p.c1.text: Right. Only the pieces of the bag were copied, not the four marbles, so the balance tips.

p.c2.text: Right. Three copies of each whole pan: still level, and the pieces make two bags and twelve marbles.

p.c3.text: Right. Twelve off both pans leaves two bags and six marbles: one bag balances three. And two thirds of three, plus four, is six.

p.done.text: That's a proof: three claims, each with its reason, and the balance backs every one. Maya multiplied only some of the terms.
